question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

Also MS-TRADE-2026-10-21-IN-01#2 quotes Jeremy France at Morgan Stanley about retirement benefits, plan sponsors. But no mention of mass-affluent in that chunk.

Also the adjacent chunk has a Morgan Stanley executive quote about retirement/401(k) plan sponsors — but not mass-affluent, and it's a statement by a firm executive about retirement benefits. That could be a partial: firm statement touching retirement plan participants but not mass-affluent specifically. Hmm.

Which to pick? The sub-question is about "statements about mass-affluent clients" — recency. I think the safest: label different_quantity with the Cerulli industry figure, since no MS statement about mass-affluent exists and the closest is an industry statistic mentioning mass-affluent. Alternatively not_found.

Given the instruction "When unsure between fact and different_quantity, choose different_quantity and say why" — that's only for fact vs different_quantity. Here unsure between different_quantity and not_found.

The Cerulli figure is an industry figure about mass-affluent participants without an advisor — related to the segment but not a firm figure nor a firm statement. Hmm, "an industry figure for a firm's own figure" — that requires the firm's own figure exists. Here no firm figure.

I lean not_found: no Morgan Stanley statement about mass-affluent clients in passages. But we could also include items? not_found requires empty items presumably.

Actually maybe include the MS trade passage and the Jeremy France quote as a different_quantity item? I'd say that's a related-but-different statement: a firm statement about retirement plan participants/employees, not mass-affluent clients.

Hmm. Decision: label different_quantity, items: two items — (1) Cerulli stat about mass-affluent participants (industry figure, not firm's statement), (2) Jeremy France quote about retirement benefits/plan sponsors (a Morgan Stanley statement about retirement plan participants, not mass-affluent clients). differs_because explaining.

Actually is including the Cerulli item appropriate given the sub-question asks about the firm's statements? It says "no passage states the asked quantity, but one states a different, related quantity." Yes, that's the situation. I'll go with different_quantity and both items, explaining.

Hmm, but should I include both? Simpler: include both with clear differs_because.

items.text: Citing Cerulli Associates, a passage reports that 63% of active 401(k) participants do not have a financial advisor and that 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor name their retirement savings account provider as their primary source of retirement planning guidance — an industry statistic, not a Morgan Stanley statement about its mass-affluent clients.
items.quote: A June 2025 Cerulli Associates report found that 63% of active 401(k) participants do not have a financial advisor , while 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor say their retirement savings account provider is their primary source of retirement planning guidance.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Jeremy France, Head of Institutional Consulting Solutions, said retirement benefits are having a marquee moment and that when plan sponsors say employees value 401(k)s on par with healthcare it signals a shift in how financial security and workplace benefits are defined — a firm statement about retirement plan sponsors and participants, not about mass-affluent clients.
items.quote: Jeremy France, Head of Institutional Consulting Solutions at Morgan Stanley, said: "Retirement benefits are having a marquee moment. When plan sponsors say they think employees value 401(k)s on par with healthcare, it signals a fundamental shift in how we define both financial security and workplace benefits."
items.scope: Institutional Consulting Solutions, retirement plan sponsors

cells.differs_because: No passage records a Morgan Stanley statement about mass-affluent clients; the closest material is an industry survey statistic about mass-affluent 401(k) participants (Cerulli) and a firm executive's statement about retirement plan sponsors and employees generally, neither of which is the firm's own statement about mass-affluent clients.
cells.reason: The passages mention mass-affluent only in an outside industry survey and give only a broader firm statement about retirement plan participants, so the asked firm statement is not stated.
